reviewer: Claude, in a Claude Code session (2026-11-14)
verdict_note: 3 critical finding(s). Not ready to issue.

mandates.text: Continuous exterior insulation on all opaque walls and roof edges; no uninsulated parapets.
Exposed sheet metal is prefinished aluminium, colour to match window frames.
No exposed sealant as the primary line of water defence.

missing: dimensions for parapet height and coping overhang

summary: The parapet is a single uninsulated block wall with a flat coping and a 4 in membrane upturn. Three items would let water in. Three more fail the code or the project mandates.

qc_list.item: Coping or cap slopes back to the roof side and has a drip edge clear of both wall faces.
qc_list.why: A flat or outward-sloping cap holds water and stains or wets the facade.
qc_list.note: Coping drawn flat with no drip.

qc_list.item: Roof membrane base flashing turns up the parapet at least 8 in (200 mm) above the finished roof surface and is terminated and counter-flashed.
qc_list.why: Low or unterminated base flashing is the most common parapet leak.
qc_list.note: Upturn labelled 4 in; no termination or counter-flashing.

qc_list.item: A continuous membrane or sheet-metal underlayment runs over the top of the parapet, under the coping, lapped onto both faces.
qc_list.why: Coping joints leak; the layer below is what keeps water out of the wall.
qc_list.note: Nothing drawn between coping and block.

qc_list.item: Air and water barrier of the wall is shown continuous with the roof membrane across the parapet.
qc_list.why: A break here lets interior air into the parapet, where it condenses.
qc_list.note: No air or water barrier is drawn on the wall.

qc_list.item: Continuous insulation wraps the parapet or the thermal break at the roof-to-wall line is shown; R-value meets the energy code for the project climate zone.
qc_list.why: An uninsulated parapet is a thermal bridge around the whole roof.
qc_list.note: Wall insulation stops at the roof slab.

qc_list.item: Cant or tapered edge, fastening of the coping (continuous cleat) and the wood blocking are labelled, with a scale and material tags.
qc_list.why: The builder needs these to price and build it; missing labels become RFIs.
qc_list.note: No cleat, blocking, cant or scale.

qc_list.item: Parapet bracing or reinforcing is shown or referenced to structural where the building is in a high seismic design category.
qc_list.why: Unbraced parapets are a falling hazard in an earthquake.
qc_list.note: No reinforcing or bracing shown or referenced; project is seismic design category D.

qc_list.item: Project mandate: Continuous exterior insulation on all opaque walls and roof edges; no uninsulated parapets.
qc_list.note: Same as RP-5: the parapet has no exterior insulation.

qc_list.item: Project mandate: Exposed sheet metal is prefinished aluminium, colour to match window frames.
Project mandate: No exposed sealant as the primary line of water defence.
qc_list.note: No sealant joint is drawn as a water line, so there is nothing to point to.

qc_list.item: Lesson learned: Coping joints opened after two winters where no membrane ran under the cap. Always draw the under-coping membrane and tag it.
qc_list.note: Same as RP-3: no membrane under the coping.

qc_list.item: Lesson learned: Parapets under 12 in high leave no room for an 8 in base flashing plus counter-flashing. Check the parapet height against the tapered insulation high point.
qc_list.note: Parapet height is not dimensioned, so the room for an 8 in base flashing cannot be checked.

qc_list.item: Lesson learned: Details issued without a scale or material tags produced the most RFIs. Tag every hatch.

findings.title: Membrane upturn is 4 in, not terminated
findings.issue: The roof membrane turns up the parapet only 4 in and ends with no termination bar or counter-flashing. Ponding water or wind-driven rain gets behind it.
findings.recommendation: Carry the base flashing at least 8 in above the finished roof, fasten it with a termination bar and cover it with counter-flashing, or run the membrane up and over the parapet.

findings.title: Coping is flat and has no drip edge
findings.issue: The coping is drawn level and flush with both wall faces. Water sits on it and runs down the cladding and the block.
findings.recommendation: Slope the coping to the roof side, extend it past both faces and add drip edges. Show the continuous cleat.

findings.title: No membrane under the coping
findings.issue: The coping sits directly on open block. Every coping joint is a leak path into the cores of the wall.
findings.recommendation: Add a continuous membrane over sloped wood blocking on top of the parapet, lapped down both faces, before the coping.

findings.title: Parapet is an uninsulated thermal bridge
findings.issue: Exterior insulation stops at the roof slab. The parapet above it is bare block. That breaks project mandate PM-1 (continuous exterior insulation, no uninsulated parapets).
findings.recommendation: Continue the exterior insulation up the outside face to the top of the parapet and insulate the roof side, or add a structural thermal break at the roof line.

findings.title: Air and water barrier not shown across the roof-to-wall line
findings.issue: No wall air barrier is drawn, so there is nothing for the roof membrane to tie into.
findings.recommendation: Draw the wall air and water barrier and show it lapped to the roof membrane over the parapet.

findings.title: Parapet reinforcing or bracing not shown
findings.issue: The block parapet has no reinforcing, bracing or structural reference. The project is in seismic design category D.
findings.recommendation: Show the reinforcing or reference the structural detail for the parapet.

findings.title: No scale, cleat, blocking or cant
findings.issue: The detail has no scale and leaves out the coping cleat, the wood blocking and the cant at the roof edge.
findings.recommendation: Add the scale and tag each item.

control_layers.note: The roof membrane stops 4 in up the parapet. Nothing covers the top of the wall.
No air barrier is drawn on the wall or across the roof line.
Roof insulation and wall insulation do not meet: the parapet between them is bare block.
No vapor control layer is drawn or named.
